title: Short Stuff: Toronto Clown Riot
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Toronto Clown Riot of July 1855. Circus clowns from the Sands/Star Troupe (described as the S.B. House Star Troop menagerie and circus from New York State) visited a brothel run by Marianne Armstrong at King and John Streets, where the Hook and Ladder fire brigade hung out. A brawl broke out between clowns and firefighters, one firefighter was seriously injured, and the next day Orange Order men attacked the circus. Hook and Ladder firefighters set fires, burned tents, and tipped wagons into the lake. Mayor (Quimby) stepped in, reportedly grabbing an axe from a rioter; police were corrupt and did not intervene. Seventeen people were charged with rioting. The riot is seen as a turning point leading to the end of Orange Order dominance over Toronto government and police, through reform. Hosts also discuss Toronto's history, the Massey Hall tour stop, and jokes about the Insane Clown Posse and Juggalos.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short episode with Chuck and a guest host filling in for Dave; brief chatter about the sound effects and the Toronto title.

segments.title: Toronto connections and tour banter
segments.summary: Hosts talk about Toronto as a favorite town, an upcoming Massey Hall show on a Canadian tour, and their first live show in Toronto.

segments.title: Toronto in 1855 and the circus arrives
segments.summary: Toronto in 1855 had many drinking establishments and brothels. The S.B. House Star Troop menagerie and circus from New York State arrived in July 1855, and its clowns went to a brothel after a long day of performing.

segments.title: Marianne Armstrong's brothel and rival private fire brigades
segments.summary: The clowns went to Marianne Armstrong's brothel at King and John Streets, the hangout of the Hook and Ladder fire brigade. Before city government ran fire services, private fire companies raced to fires and sometimes fought each other. A few weeks earlier, Hook and Ladder had been in a riot at a burning house where firefighters let the house burn and looted nearby homes.

segments.title: Brawl breaks out at the brothel
segments.summary: The clowns and firefighters were drinking at the brothel when a fight broke out. Accounts generally say the clowns started it, possibly by cutting in line or knocking over a firefighter's drink.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the outcome of the brawl is revealed.

segments.title: Outcome of the brawl and the Orange Order
segments.summary: The clowns won: a firefighter was seriously injured and the firefighters retreated. Toronto was run for over a hundred years by the Orange Order, an Irish Protestant fraternal group whose members held elected office, police, and firefighting jobs. The Hook and Ladder company were Orangemen.

segments.title: Aside on Orangemen and Syracuse
segments.summary: A brief joking tangent comparing the Orangemen to Syracuse, with no factual conclusion reached.

segments.title: Next-day Orange Order attack on the circus
segments.summary: Word of the fight spread and Orange Order men attacked the circus the next day, throwing rocks and beating clowns while the crowd grew. Hook and Ladder firefighters set fires, burned tents, used fire axes on the circus property, and tipped performers' wagons into the lake.

segments.title: Mayor Quimby, the police, and the riot's name
segments.summary: The circus was overwhelmed until Mayor Quimby arrived and reportedly grabbed an axe from a rioter. The police chief, an Orangeman, was credited with keeping rioters from harming the animals, but police otherwise did not intervene. The hosts discuss the name Toronto Clown Riot or Toronto circus riot.

segments.title: Aftermath and circus leaves town
segments.summary: The mob dispersed, and the circus people gathered their things and left Toronto for Ottawa.

segments.title: Band name and Juggalos tangent
segments.summary: The hosts joke about using Toronto Clown Riot as a band name, referencing Insane Clown Posse and Juggalos.

segments.title: Charges, reform, and end of Orange Order rule
segments.summary: Seventeen people were charged with rioting, though corruption limited a wider crackdown. The riot was seen as a last straw that led the Reform Party into power, and it took about a hundred years to remove the Orange Order from power. Adam Bunch in Spacing magazine calls the riot a turning point toward a less corrupt police force.

segments.title: Orangeman handshake joke
segments.summary: Light closing banter in which Josh jokes about a secret Orangeman handshake for spotting Orange men among police, and Chuck jokes about squeezing skin.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck closes the episode with the standard iHeartRadio production credit.
